extracted.intended_audience: Sage developers and contributors who review or submit GitHub pull requests
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for developers performing peer review of code changes (PRs) to the Sage codebase, including what to check before marking a PR as ready and rules for release inclusion and PR closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require GitHub checks have passed
rubrics_metrics.description: We require all checks have passed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before reviewing a PR ensure that the automated GitHub checks (build/test checks) are green. A failed check is a blocker to positive review until resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the diff (Files changed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Click “Files changed” tab of the PR. Read through the changes of all modified files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pull request review tools to add comments directly to changed lines. Ensure you understand every change in the diff rather than relying only on descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test the code locally when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Checkout the code of the PR and run the relevant tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing is optional if build-and-test check passed, but reviewers should run reproducible tests for suspicious/complex changes. Follow repository instructions for checking out PR branches and running test suites.

rubrics_metrics.name: The purpose / correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the code address the PR’s stated aim? Can it introduce any new problems?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test the new or fixed functionality with a variety of input (not just documentation examples) to confirm expected, robust output and absence of unexpected errors or crashes. Consider corner cases and mathematical correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: User documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the use of the new code clear to a user?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that mathematical notions are standard or are explained/linked; ensure users can find and use the new code easily. Documentation should be sufficient for intended users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code documentation (inline comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the code sufficiently commented so that a developer does not have to wonder what exactly it does?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should clarify non-obvious algorithms, invariants, and design choices. Avoid leaving future reviewers confused about intent or behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect project and language conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the code respect Sage’s conventions? Python’s conventions? Cython’s conventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow established style and structural conventions for the project and languages used; nonconforming code should be requested to be changed or justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Do all functions contain doctests?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sage-coverage <files> to check. Ensure all aspects of new/modified methods and classes are tested with doctests (see 'Writing testable examples'). Missing doctests should be requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bugfixes must include demonstrative doctests
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PR contains a bugfix, does it add a doctest illustrating that the bug has been fixed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New doctest should include the issue or PR number (example: See :issue:`12345`). This provides regression protection and traceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance / speedup claims must be demonstrable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PR claims to speed up some computation, does the PR contain code examples to illustrate the claim?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the speedup is achieved and provide reproducible examples/benchmarks. Also check whether the PR unintentionally makes other code slower.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference manual builds without errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the reference manual build without errors (check both html and pdf)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should attempt to build the manuals (see The Sage Manuals) to ensure no build errors are introduced by the PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference manual looks correct (formatting/links)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the reference manual look okay? Typos may allow builds but cause badly formatted output or broken hyperlinks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect rendered manuals for formatting issues and broken links even when builds succeed. Request fixes for problems that harm documentation quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run all relevant tests including long doctests
rubrics_metrics.description: Do all doctests pass without errors? Unrelated components of Sage may be affected by the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check tests across the whole library, including 'long' doctests (use make ptestlong) and optional doctests related to the functionality. See Running Sage’s Doctests for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual testing for UI/interactive changes
rubrics_metrics.description: For changes that affect the user interface (e.g., IPython/Jupyter components), manual testing is crucial because automatic tests do not cover UI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a Jupyter notebook with comprehensive tests of graphics and typesetting (some of which are Sage-specific). Manually verify interactive behavior where automated tests are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set PR status appropriately (positive/needs work/needs info)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide PR status after checks: positive review if questions answered; needs work if problems; needs info if clarifications required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If answers to review questions are 'yes' set positive. If something is wrong, list points to address and set needs work. If unclear, ask question and set needs info. If uncertain about final decision, explain what you did and request another reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid feature requests / scope creep during review
rubrics_metrics.description: The point of the review is to ensure guidelines are followed and implementation is mathematically correct. Refrain from additional feature requests or open-ended discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want the code written differently, make a clear, actionable request rather than open-ended feature discussion. 'The perfect is the enemy of the good.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Closing PRs and using resolution labels
rubrics_metrics.description: PRs can be closed when they have positive review or for other reasons; use one of the resolution labels r:duplicate, r:invalid, r:wontfix, r:worksforme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When closing for reasons other than positive review add a comment explaining why the PR was closed if not already clear. Reopen if closure was premature.

rubrics_metrics.name: One issue per PR / issue
rubrics_metrics.description: An issue must cover only one issue and should not be a laundry list of unrelated issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an issue covers multiple independent problems, it cannot be cleanly closed and may leave parts unresolved; split into separate issues/PRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'patch bombs' (very large PRs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit huge bundles that rip out subsystems and replace them (patch bombs are problematic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer small, gradual changes that are easy to review and apply. If a large rewrite is unavoidable, be aware review will be tedious and may be rejected or delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sage-specific policy: do not replace core components with external packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage ships everything in one source tarball; replacing essential components (e.g., Pari, GAP, Lisp, GMP) with external packages is discouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a distribution package is buggy, file a bug with that package. Sage maintainers may help but there are no guarantees; PRs that attempt to replace core components may be invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: No support-discussion issues
rubrics_metrics.description: GitHub is not meant for general usage support queries; an issue should be clearly a bug and not 'How do I do X?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redirect user-support questions to sage-support. If a genuine bug is identified, open a concise, to-the-point PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solutions must be achievable and measurable
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues must be achievable and not vague grand goals (e.g., 'Make Sage the best CAS in the world').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require objectives with metrics or actionable scope. Vague, subjective goals are inappropriate for tracker issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beta release inclusion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For preparing a new beta or first release candidate, all positively reviewed PRs with the forthcoming release milestone are considered; Release Manager merges PRs in batches of 10–20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a merge conflict occurs the PR is set back to 'needs work'; authors may declare dependencies or resolve conflicts before re-requesting positive review. Each batch undergoes integration testing; problematic PRs are unmerged and set back to needs work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release candidate stage: only blocker PRs considered
rubrics_metrics.description: After the first release candidate, only PRs with priority set to 'blocker' are considered; PRs with other priorities are ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a PR is important enough for inclusion at this stage set p:blocker/1 label and explain rationale on the PR. Other priorities (including 'critical') are not sufficient for inclusion in this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blocker priority guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Blocker PRs should be used sparingly; merging has a risk/benefit trade-off since code changes can introduce new problems and delay release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale on the PR for blocker status. Generally new features and large refactorings are not blockers unless they are essential to the release focus. Be aware that a problematic blocker can delay release by up to two weeks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final release condition
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no blocker PR for the last release candidate, the Release Manager turns it to the final release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final release is tagged with the release milestone and announced on sage-release. Release management scripts are maintained in sagemath/sage-release-management repository.
